strengths: Novel problem identification with strong empirical evidence: Quantifies capability degradation as a real phenomenon (62.33%/55.80% R@1 vs 100% for foundation model on solvable subsets)
Well-motivated solution design: Diagnose-generate-refine pipeline strategically targets decision boundaries rather than indiscriminate scaling, demonstrated by Random Mining comparison
Strong experimental results: Achieves SOTA on CIRR (55.52% R@1 vs 53.64% for CIR-LVLM) and FashionIQ (57.04% avg R@10), with substantial improvements over baseline (8.38% and 7.16% respectively)
Comprehensive ablation studies: Progressive validation (Table 4) and Random Mining baseline (Table 3) clearly demonstrate the contribution of each component with proper statistical reporting
Generalizability across model backbones: Validated effectiveness on both Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B, showing the approach works even with stronger foundation models
Data efficiency: Focused diagnosis demonstrates superior efficiency compared to blind synthesis, maximizing gradient signal per synthetic triplet
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Individual components are well-established (CoT prompting, VQA filtering, triplet loss, contrastive learning); grouped contrastive refinement is a straightforward batching strategy without fundamental innovation

Critical implementation details missing for reproducibility: Intent Decomposition & Verification procedures lack specificity; exact prompts, minimal edit constraints, VQA confidence thresholds, and top-K selection values not provided; code not available despite reliance on MLLM prompting quality

Insufficient analysis of method mechanics: No reporting of VQA filtering rates to assess quality control effectiveness; missing sensitivity analysis for prompt variations, hyperparameter K, or quality thresholds; no systematic failure case analysis beyond 2 qualitative examples

Computational cost unaddressed: Foundation model must be run for every training instance (mining + generation + verification); no quantification of training time, resource overhead, or FLOPs compared to baseline—critical for practical applicability

Narrow evaluation scope: Only two closely related datasets (fashion e-commerce and NLVR2-derived); no evaluation on other compositional reasoning tasks; generalization to significantly different domains unclear; model-agnostic claim only validated on Qwen family

Incomplete comparative analysis: No investigation of whether capability degradation exists in other MLLM adaptations (CIR-LVLM, etc.); missing VQA-based retrieval vs embedding-based tradeoff comparison; no comparison with alternative self-improvement strategies

Experimental design concerns: Inconsistent hyperparameters across datasets without justification; arbitrary 'Avg.' metric definition; only 4 random seeds for Random Mining; no statistical significance testing for main results; missing ablations on loss weight sensitivity
Overstated claims: 'Model-agnostic' claim unsupported (Qwen variants only); 'paradigm conflict' never formally defined; applicability beyond retrieval tasks unexplored

strengths: Clear and well-motivated identification of capability degradation phenomenon with strong empirical evidence (Figure 1: 62.33% vs. 100% R@1)
Comprehensive experimental validation including thorough ablations, cross-backbone generalization, and cross-model transfer studies demonstrating model-agnostic applicability
Strong empirical results achieving state-of-the-art on CIRR (+8.38% R@1) and FashionIQ (+7.16% avg R@10) with consistent improvements
Practical and efficient framework with reasonable one-time offline synthesis cost (10-14h) and comparable refinement training time
Extensive qualitative analysis including failure case studies, triplet synthesis visualizations, and interpretable examples demonstrating what the model learns
Thorough supplementary material with prompt details, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, computational breakdowns, and reproducibility information
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: combines existing techniques (self-guided mining, CoT generation, VQA filtering, triplet loss) without significant algorithmic innovation

Shallow theoretical understanding of capability degradation: identifies the phenomenon but doesn't explain the underlying mechanism (representation collapse, loss mismatch, etc.). Table 8 shows increasing capacity worsens performance but lacks mechanistic analysis
Narrow experimental scope: evaluation limited to two CIR datasets in similar domains (fashion/open-domain). No evidence of generalization to other retrieval tasks or domains

Data quality and reliability concerns: VQA-based filtering achieves only 92% accuracy (~8% noise), assumption that foundation model F always provides correct reasoning contradicted by Section 8.3 failure analysis showing F has residual weaknesses
Heavy reliance on prompt engineering with reproducibility concerns: code link redacted, results likely sensitive to prompt wording variations, unclear how to adapt to different MLLM versions
Incomplete analysis of when/why approach fails: Section 8.3 identifies ambiguous instructions and spatial reasoning challenges with no proposed solutions, suggesting fundamental limitations
Incremental performance gains (7-8% on R@1) may not justify the added complexity of four-stage pipeline and offline data synthesis

Unresolved methodological questions: unclear if grouped contrastive strategy risks model preferring corrected variants on all data, minimal edit principle enforced only via prompting without systematic verification

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with compelling quantitative evidence (Figure 1: 62.33% vs 100% R@1 gap showing capability degradation)
Comprehensive experimental validation: consistent improvements on CIRR (+8.38% R@1) and FashionIQ (+7.16% avg R@10) with detailed ablation studies
Thoughtful methodology: self-guided mining outperforms random mining (57.04% vs 53.80%), validating the diagnose-first approach
Strong reproducibility: extensive supplementary details including full prompts (Fig. 15), hyperparameter grids, computational costs, and human evaluation of quality control (92% accuracy)
Cross-backbone generalization demonstrated (Qwen2.5-VL-7B to Qwen3-VL-8B), supporting model-agnostic claims
Clear presentation with effective qualitative examples (Figs. 9-14) and well-structured methodology
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: core contribution is sophisticated data augmentation; self-improvement and hard negative mining for MLLMs are well-established (STaR, Self-Refine, Reflexion)
Shallow mechanistic understanding: 'paradigm conflict' is loosely defined with no formal analysis of why fine-tuning degrades compositional reasoning or what representational properties are lost

Circular reasoning risk: ReCALL uses foundation model F to generate corrective data, then trains R_refine, but R_refine inherits the same reasoning from F—lacks analysis of whether improvement comes from better data curation vs. actual capability recalibration

Methodological gaps: (1) Hard Negative Mining comparison (52.57%) confounded by lack of VQA verification; (2) VQA quality control removes 8.5-10.4% of data with 8% residual noise—impact not analyzed; (3) hyperparameter sensitivity shown but not justified (λ varies by dataset)
Limited experimental scope: single primary backbone (Qwen2.5-VL-7B), only two structurally similar datasets (CIRR, FashionIQ), no evaluation on other retrieval tasks despite 'model-agnostic' claims

Unaddressed failure modes (Section 8.3) indicate fundamental limitations inherited from foundation model: false negatives from annotation sparsity, ambiguous instructions, weak spatial reasoning—ReCALL doesn't resolve these
Modest absolute gains on key metrics (R@50: +0.36% CIRR, +1.37% FashionIQ) and computational cost barrier (14.2h offline generation) not adequately discussed for practical impact
Incomplete alternatives comparison: no ablation using dedicated retriever trained from scratch on larger datasets; limited exploration of alternatives beyond Random/Hard Negative mining
Cross-model transfer modest (+1.15% vs +2.72% full pipeline in Table 6) suggests model-specific overfitting; transferability to other retrieval tasks not demonstrated

Missing analyses: representation-space properties (embedding similarity distributions), CoT complexity sensitivity, one-to-many evaluation to mitigate false negatives, theoretical justification for loss combination

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: Capability degradation is clearly articulated with compelling quantitative evidence (R@1 of 62.33% on F-solvable instances) and qualitative examples showing fine-grained reasoning failures in adapted models
Coherent three-stage framework: The diagnose-generate-refine pipeline is logically structured with clear motivation for each component and elegant integration into a unified approach

Comprehensive experimental validation: Thorough ablations isolating each component, Random Mining comparison demonstrating diagnosis efficiency, cross-backbone generalization studies, data scale analysis, hyperparameter sensitivity, and transparent computational cost reporting
Consistent state-of-the-art results: 55.52% R@1 on CIRR (+8.38% over baseline) and 57.04% avg R@10 on FashionIQ (+7.16% over baseline) with improvements across all major metrics
Practical and generalizable design: Model-agnostic framework demonstrated on multiple MLLMs, one-time offline synthesis amortizing computational costs, and reasonable efficiency trade-offs

Extensive analysis and transparency: Rich supplementary material with detailed visualizations of the pipeline on real examples (Figs. 13-14), honest failure case analysis, human evaluation of VQA filtering (92% accuracy), and cross-model transfer experiments
Clear presentation: Well-written paper with effective figures, logical flow, and thorough documentation enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Individual components (instance mining from failures, CoT generation, grouped contrastive learning, VQA filtering) are largely standard techniques; contribution is primarily integration rather than novel methodology

Insufficient theoretical understanding: While 'paradigm conflict' between generation and discrimination is identified, the paper lacks formal analysis of what capabilities degrade, why they degrade, and which reasoning patterns are most affected. Needs embedding space analysis or attention visualization of the degradation mechanism
Modest improvements over concurrent work: Only 1.88% absolute gain over CIR-LVLM on CIRR and 0.83% on FashionIQ, suggesting incremental rather than substantial progress despite strong baselines

Heavy dependence on foundation model quality: Framework's performance ceiling is limited by foundation model's zero-shot capabilities; acknowledged spatial reasoning weaknesses (Fig. 12, Case 3) demonstrate error inheritance; limited analysis of which degradation types can be recovered vs. cannot

Synthetic data reliability concerns: VQA filtering achieves 92% accuracy (not 100%) on sampled triplets; no analysis of failure modes, error types, or cumulative effects when training on mixed synthetic/original data; missing sensitivity analysis on filtering accuracy impact

Narrow evaluation breadth: Only two CIR benchmarks evaluated; unclear if findings generalize to other vision-language tasks, adaptation scenarios, or different domains; no comparison with alternative adaptation strategies or baseline approaches

Computational cost practicality: 14.2 hours generation time for CIRR plus filtering is substantial; may be prohibitive for practitioners with new datasets; requires access to capable models and GPUs; amortization argument only holds for repeated use on same data

Incomplete ablations and missing comparisons: Baseline uses only InfoNCE loss (no exploration of alternatives); prompt engineering impact underexplored despite lengthy Section 7; no systematic analysis of informative instances per query; missing comparison with simpler alternatives like standard hard negative mining

Failure case attribution deflection: Most reported failures blamed on dataset annotation sparsity and inherent ambiguity rather than method limitations; raises question of what percentage of errors are truly method-driven vs. dataset-driven

Statistical rigor limitations: Most results lack confidence intervals or significance testing; single-run evaluations vulnerable to random seed effects; no statistical comparison with concurrent methods beyond point estimates

Reproducibility gaps: Code availability placeholder not filled; VQA confidence thresholds and exact filtering criteria incompletely specified; hyperparameter K selected without clear justification; heavy dependence on specific model (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) with limited sensitivity analysis
